findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size now uses single-brace placeholders and Java ChoiceFormat in an i18next-consumed bundle
findings.body: This file is consumed by the React account console via i18next, which is why every other entry uses double-brace interpolation (e.g. "error-username-invalid-character='{{0}}' contains invalid character." on line 14) and <0>-style Trans component tags (line 13). The new value "Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}." uses single braces, which i18next does not interpolate, and Java MessageFormat choice syntax, which i18next cannot evaluate. If this key is rendered in the account UI, users will see the literal text "{0}", "{1}" and "{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}" instead of a formatted message. The Java-side MessageFormat version belongs in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages (where {0} is correct), not in the keycloak.v3 JS bundle.

findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size changed to Java ChoiceFormat syntax in the admin console JS message bundle
findings.body: The keycloak.v2 admin messages bundle is loaded by the admin console's JS i18n layer (i18next), not by Java MessageFormat. Replacing "value(s)" with "{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}" means the admin UI cannot render this validation message: the choice expression will be displayed literally to administrators, and single-brace {0}/{1}/{2} placeholders are not interpolated by i18next's default {{...}} syntax. The MessageFormat variant should only live in the server-side theme bundles (themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/admin/messages and themes/src/main/resources-community/...), not in this JS resource.

findings.title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: totpStep1 was changed from a Lithuanian translation to the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". Lithuanian users of the account theme's authenticator setup page will now be shown instructions in Italian. It should read e.g. "Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:".

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: loginTotpStep1 in the Lithuanian login theme was replaced with the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" instead of a Lithuanian translation, so the OTP setup page of the login theme will show Italian text to Lithuanian users.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese file updated with Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: totpStep1 was changed to "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：", which is Traditional Chinese (機/應/個), in the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) account bundle. The correct Simplified rendering would be "在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：". This is consistent with the original text being copied from a zh_TW/zh_HK source rather than translated.

findings.title: English reference bundle located via fragile path string rewriting; missing counterpart crashes the mojo with a raw RuntimeException
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file by running replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") and replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties") on the absolute file path, then does "new FileInputStream(englishFile)" and throws a bare RuntimeException on IOException (lines 76-80). Two problems: (1) any messages file that exists only under resources-community (or under a JS module theme whose product counterpart is absent) has no derived _en sibling, so the whole verification build aborts with "unable to read file ..." instead of reporting a per-file message like the rest of the checker; (2) the replaceAll of "resources-community" operates on the entire absolute path, so any other occurrence of that substring (e.g. in a checkout/workspace directory name) silently corrupts the resolved path. Failure to locate the English bundle should degrade to a reported message (or MojoExecutionException), not an uncaught RuntimeException, and the mapping should be done on the file name/directory structure explicitly.

findings.title: Anchor check requires anchors to appear in the same order and byte-identical form as the English source
findings.body: santizeAnchors() walks anchors in the translation and the English value in parallel and only accepts a pair when matcher.group() equals englishMatcher.group() exactly. A legitimate translation that reorders two links within one message (common when sentence structure differs), or that differs in attribute quoting/spacing inside the <a> tag while keeping the same href, will be rejected with "Didn't find anchor tag ..." even though it contains exactly the anchors from the source. This will produce false build failures for future translation contributions and push translators toward keeping English word order.

findings.title: No positive test: valid HTML matching the English source should produce no messages
findings.body:
All new tests assert that violations are detected (illegal tag, HTML without English counterpart, changed anchor). There is no test that a translation containing exactly the anchors and allowed tags (/

//
) present in the English source yields an empty message list. Without such a passing-case test, a regression in the normalization/unescaping pipeline that makes the checker flag every file with HTML (e.g. the "" stripping or the unescapeHtml4 round-trip) would not be caught by the suite.
